guard_streams.source: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q4 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Provider-level complaint findings are service-quality indicators and cannot verify physical availability or parcel-specific network performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Q4 2025 complaints findings on 11 May 2026.
The figures cover October to December 2025.
Overall complaints increased quarter-on-quarter for the first time since 2023.
Broadband complaints decreased.
Landline complaints decreased.
Pay-TV complaints stayed the same.
Mobile complaints increased after mid-contract price-rise announcements by some providers.
TalkTalk and Vodafone were the most complained-about broadband providers.
Plusnet and Virgin Media were the least complained-about broadband providers.
O2 generated the most mobile complaints, mainly about contract-related issues.

guard_streams.write_limit: The Communications Market portal contains aggregate market, industry and consumer-research data, not exact current selected-parcel coverage or measured speed.

facts.detail: The Communications Market 2025 portal was published on 17 July 2025.
The report is delivered as an interactive data portal.
The portal includes data collected from industry by Ofcom.
It includes data from Ofcom consumer research.
It includes headline figures from selected third parties.
Related analysis is available in Media Nations.
Related analysis is available in Online Nation.
Infrastructure analysis is available in Connected Nations.
Ofcom published a short PDF summary of key findings.
The data-download section includes a telecoms-data CSV.

guard_streams.write_limit: Operator deployment plans are forward-looking and confidence-qualified; they cannot be treated as current selected-parcel serviceability or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the 2026 planned-network-deployments report on 13 May 2026.
The report is based on operator plans as of January 2026.
It covers planned deployments over the following three years to January 2029.
The dataset includes privately funded and publicly supported operator plans.
It does not separately count rollout aspirations of public authorities.
If all plans are realised, full fibre could reach 28.1 million homes, or 92 percent, by January 2029.
Gigabit-capable coverage could reach 29 million homes, or 95 percent.
High-confidence full-fibre plans imply 87 percent by January 2028 and 88 percent by January 2029.
Rural gigabit-capable coverage could rise from 66 percent to 86 percent.
Operators planned or proposed upgrades to around 6,950 geographically distinct FWA masts.
